sections.h2: Where is Howard County, Indiana, and which towns does it include?
sections.html:
Howard County is in north central Indiana, and Kokomo is both the county seat and its largest city. The county covers 293.92 square miles, almost all of it land, and touches Miami County to the north, Grant to the east, Tipton to the south, Clinton to the southwest, Carroll to the west and Cass to the northwest.

Beyond Kokomo, the communities people name most often are Greentown, Russiaville and Indian Heights, along with the unincorporated community of Cassville. Wildcat Creek and the Kokomo (Wildcat Creek) Reservoir are the county's best-known water features.

Indiana organized the county in 1844 as Richardville County. It was renamed in 1846 for U.S. Representative Tilghman Howard. About 74 percent of residents live in areas counted as urban.

sections.h2: What do Kokomo's employers mean for people who own houses here?
sections.html:
Manufacturing, and automotive work in particular, is the backbone of local employment. Kokomo grew up around natural gas and railroads, and Elwood Haynes test-drove an early automobile here in 1894.

The employers named in the Wikipedia article on Kokomo give a sense of scale:

  • Stellantis Kokomo Transmission Plant, listed at 3,583 employees
  • Indiana Transmission Plants I and II, listed at 2,439 employees
  • Kokomo Casting Plant, listed at 1,281 employees
  • Kokomo Engine Plant, where production began in 2022
  • StarPlus Energy, a joint venture of Stellantis and Samsung SDI, plus BorgWarner, GM Components Holdings and Haynes International

Those headcounts are the figures the article reports, so treat them as approximate. Many households here depend on a handful of plants, which makes local hiring and plant news matter to housing demand.

sections.h2: What weather and storm history should Howard County sellers know?
sections.html:
Kokomo has a humid continental climate, with about 44.4 inches of precipitation and 34.1 inches of snow in an average year (1991 to 2020 normals). January afternoons average roughly 32.5 degrees and July afternoons roughly 83.7 degrees.

Tornadoes are part of the local record. An F4 tornado struck the southern part of Kokomo on April 11, 1965, killed 25 people in the area and heavily damaged the Chrysler transmission plant and several schools. Two tornadoes hit the north side on April 20, 2004. On August 24, 2016, an EF3 tornado damaged about 1,000 homes on the south side and destroyed 80.

If you own a house with old storm damage, a roof near the end of its life or a repair that was never finished, that condition shows up in an appraisal and in a buyer's inspection.

sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Howard County?
sections.html:
Three offices in the Howard County Administration Center, 220 North Main Street in Kokomo, share the work: the assessor sets value, the auditor keeps the deduction and tax sale records, and the treasurer collects the money. All three list weekday hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

The assessor also acts as secretary to the county Property Tax Assessment Board of Appeals. A separate Center Township Assessor page exists on the county site. The assessor's office says it is reassessing eastern Howard County this year, starting with Taylor Township.

sections.h2: How do Indiana's caps and deductions change a Howard County bill?
sections.html:
The rate is only part of the picture, because Indiana limits what a parcel can owe as a share of its gross assessed value. The state's circuit breaker caps are:

  • 1 percent for a homestead that receives the homestead standard deduction
  • 2 percent for other residential property, which includes single-family houses that are not homesteads and buildings with two or more dwelling units
  • 2 percent for agricultural land and 3 percent for nonresidential and personal property

The homestead standard deduction is shrinking on a schedule set by the 2025 legislation. The Department of Local Government Finance memo lists $48,000 for the 2025 assessment date, $40,000 for 2026, $30,000 for 2027 and $0 from 2030 on. A supplemental homestead deduction grows over the same years, starting at 40 percent for taxes payable in 2026 and reaching 66.7 percent in 2031.

The Howard County Auditor says a homestead application must be completed and dated by December 31, and that you do not need to reapply each year unless the property is sold, the title changes or the contract is paid off. For a buyer, that means the seller's deduction does not carry over automatically.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Howard County assessment?
sections.html:
You start with a Form 130 filed with the assessing official, one petition per parcel. The deadline is June 15 of the year tied to the notice: if the county mails Form 11 before May 1, it is June 15 of that assessment year; otherwise it is June 15 of the year the treasurer mails the bill.

After filing, the assessor schedules a preliminary informal meeting and reports the result to the county board. The board must hold a hearing within 180 days of the petition and mail notice at least 30 days ahead. If you disagree with the decision, or no decision arrives in 180 days, you can file Form 131 with the Indiana Board of Tax Review.

Two details help owners. The assessor carries the burden of proof if the value rose more than 5 percent over the prior assessment date, unless the jump came from renovation, new improvements or a change in use. And while an appeal is pending, you may pay on the previous year's assessment without penalty until it is resolved.

sections.h2: When is Howard County property tax due, and what does late cost?
sections.html:
The 2026 installments are due May 11 and November 10. Late payments carry a 5 percent charge if paid within 30 days (on a parcel with no back taxes), and the charge rises to 10 percent of the unpaid tax after that.

Indiana bills a year behind. The bill you pay in 2026 reflects ownership and value as of January 1 of the prior year, which is why a mid-year closing can leave a buyer paying a prorated share of the seller's arrears. Your closing agent sets the exact split.

The treasurer takes payments online through InvoiceCloud, at four named local banks and in a drop box to the right of the Administration Center entrance.

sections.h2: What happens when Howard County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
Parcels with delinquent taxes go to an annual tax sale. The 2026 advertisement listed 460 parcels for October 27, 2026, with a 10:00 a.m. start in the Commissioners' Meeting Room and a possible move to an online auction.

A property cannot sell for less than the delinquent taxes and special assessments, the taxes due in the sale year, penalties, $25 for postage and publication, and related county costs. The owner can still redeem after the sale:

  • 110 percent of the minimum bid if redeemed within six months, or 115 percent after that
  • Plus any overbid amount and 5 percent yearly interest on it, plus taxes the buyer paid afterward
  • For certificates sold at the 2026 sale, the redemption period ends October 27, 2027; certificates struck to the county may end February 24, 2027

Defenses had to be filed with the Howard County Circuit Court before October 9, 2026.

sections.h2: What should you gather before selling a Howard County house with tax due?
sections.html:
Collect the paper that shows exactly what is owed before you talk to any buyer. The county treasurer can tell you the amount due on a parcel, and a closing agent pays it from proceeds.

  • Your latest tax bill and the parcel number
  • Any Form 11 assessment notice and any Form 130 you filed
  • Whether the parcel appears on the certified tax sale list
  • Records of weed cut, demolition or nuisance liens the treasurer has placed
  • Your homestead deduction approval, if you claimed one

The office phone numbers above are the right place to confirm any figure before you rely on it.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill in Howard County, Indiana?
faqs.a: The Howard County Treasurer, at 220 North Main Street, Room 226 in Kokomo, collects property tax and can be reached at 765-456-2213. The assessor sets value and the auditor handles deductions, so questions about value or a missing homestead deduction go to those offices instead.

faqs.q: What are the 2026 Howard County property tax due dates?
faqs.a: May 11, 2026 and November 10, 2026. Partial payments are accepted, and the treasurer lists online, bank and drop box options.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for paying Howard County taxes late?
faqs.a: The state's schedule adds 5 percent for payment within 30 days of the due date on a parcel with no back taxes, and 10 percent of the unpaid tax after that.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Howard County assessment?
faqs.a: File Form 130 with the assessor by June 15 of the year tied to your notice, one form per parcel. If the county board's decision is unsatisfactory, Form 131 goes to the Indiana Board of Tax Review.

faqs.q: Do I need to reapply for the homestead deduction after buying a house in Howard County?
faqs.a: Yes. The auditor says you reapply when a property is sold or the title changes, and the application must be completed and dated by December 31.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Howard County house that is on the tax sale list?
faqs.a: The treasurer's page says a parcel comes off the certified list when the taxes are paid, using cash, a cashier's check or a credit card. After a tax sale, the owner can still redeem during the redemption period, which for certificates sold at the 2026 sale ends October 27, 2027.
